title: The Amen break lineage
hook: 4 bars of drums. Thousands of records. Nobody got paid.
voiceover: 4 bars of drums. Thousands of records. Nobody got paid. 1969, a Washington DC soul group called The Winstons cut a B-side, Amen, Brother. Halfway through, drummer Gregory Coleman plays 4 bars alone. That's the Amen break. It got pressed onto Ultimate Breaks and Beats, then N.W.A. ran it under Straight Outta Compton in 1988. Then UK producers chopped it into jungle and drum and bass, and it became the fastest moving drum pattern on earth. The Winstons never saw a royalty. In 2015 fans raised over 24,000 pounds for singer Richard Spencer, the first money that break ever sent home. Name a record on the Amen I missed.
caption: The Amen break: Amen, Brother by The Winstons (Metromedia, 1969), drums by Gregory Coleman. Straight Outta Compton, half of jungle, Oasis, and thousands more sit on those 4 bars. The band was never paid for a single sample; a 2015 crowdfund finally sent Richard Spencer some money. I still cut this in drum and bass rooms. Name a record on the Amen I missed and I'll pin the best one. 🥁
